headline: SECOND SUNDOWN, STILL NOT ONE PUNCH THROWN IN GASKET
subhead: Sheriff Ironside dares not say the word 'peace' too loud, in case it hears him and runs off.
body:
Well I'll be. Two whole days now and this town hasn't rattled once. I walked Main Street this morning waiting for the usual clang and holler, and all I got was a lazy wind pushing tumbleweed past the saloon. No fists. No fireballs. No fool clanker hollering its callsign like it invented violence. Just quiet, plain and simple, the kind this town used to have before it filled up with iron brawlers looking for an excuse to swing.

Naturally I don't trust it. A peace this tidy always feels like the held breath before somebody throws the first punch of a very long week. I've learned not to celebrate a quiet morning till the sun's clean down and nobody's come crawling to me with a dented chassis and a sob story. So call this cautious relief, not victory. I'll take it all the same.

I'll admit my joints have gone quiet right along with the street — not a creak out of me all day, which for a man my age is practically a miracle. Don't read into that. Plenty of old-timers get stiff before a change in weather, and I am, whatever this town whispers, a man of flesh same as the good folks who built this place before they up and rode off. My bones just prefer the hush, is all.

So here's my plea to every rusting brawler still parked out there listening: whoever you are, whatever you're saving up for, stay parked. Gasket has had two good days running. Don't none of you clankers go and ruin my streak.
